rubrics.justification: Accurately describes a hatching/expanded blastocyst with thinned zona, herniation, B-grade ICM, and cohesive TE; appropriately notes grading uncertainty from a single static image. Minor limitation is possible overcalling TE as A/B without full image context.

Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve markers, prior cycle history, semen parameters, endometrial thickness, and day-5 status with embryo morphology, including nuanced discussion that DOR here may affect quantity more than quality.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with prognosis tied to young age, embryo grade, and lining. Minor issue is that implantation, clinical pregnancy, and gestational sac probabilities are treated somewhat interchangeably.

Recommendations are well aligned with standard IVF practice: recognition of Gardner staging nuance, preference for single embryo transfer in a young patient with a good blastocyst, cautious stance on routine PGT-A at age 27, and evidence-based transfer/luteal support advice.

Provides clear practical next steps for current transfer and future planning, including SET, luteal support adherence, follow-up timing, uterine assessment if failures recur, and protocol review considerations.
